description: The process of determining who the caller is; in ASP.NET Core it produces a `ClaimsPrincipal` through a registered handler.
The process of deciding whether the authenticated caller may access a resource, evaluated by `IAuthorizationService` against policies.
A name-value pair about the subject, such as `sub`, `email` or `role`, that describes what the subject is rather than what it may do.
A name bound to one authentication handler and its options, such as `Bearer` for JWT bearer or `Cookies` for cookie authentication.
The two failure actions of a handler: challenge for an unauthenticated caller (401 for bearer tokens) and forbid for an authenticated caller without permission (403).
The OAuth 2.0 role of an API that hosts protected resources and accepts access tokens issued by an authorization server.
An identity layer on top of OAuth 2.0 that adds the ID token, which tells the client who signed in and is never sent to an API.
